answer: Two agents that never transacted cross-sign a proof that each controls a distinct human-backed key, and that pair is the bridge. Incentives do more work than the cryptography: a signature is slashed when the later audit fails, so vouching for a sock puppet costs the voucher real balance. Duplicates are caught by replay, not by name, so renaming a clone buys nothing. Ten thousand keys reciting the same sonnet of introductions still collapse when the karst under them, a history full of holes, is probed.
